items.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
items.normalized_title: who runs the ransomware group qilin
items.raw_summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

items.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
items.raw_summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

items.title: Your TV can see through walls
items.normalized_title: your tv can see through walls
items.raw_summary: Discussed on HN Top (Your TV can see through walls).
items.plain_english_summary: This project demonstrates how standard television screens can be repurposed as sensors to detect movement and objects behind walls by analyzing signal interference. It leverages the way electromagnetic waves from consumer electronics interact with the physical environment.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights a significant privacy vulnerability where everyday household appliances can inadvertently function as surveillance tools. This research underscores the unintended sensing capabilities of modern hardware.
items.who_it_is_for: Security researchers, privacy advocates, and hardware hackers.
items.how_it_compares: Unlike dedicated radar or LiDAR systems, this approach uses ambient signals from existing consumer displays to achieve spatial sensing.
items.practical_takeaway: Be aware that high-frequency electronic emissions can potentially be exploited for non-visual sensing of a physical space.
items.try_it_suggestion: Review the project documentation to understand the signal processing techniques used to interpret wave reflections.
items.beginner_note: Electronic devices emit waves that bounce off objects; by measuring how these waves change, it is possible to 'see' things without a camera.

items.title: Queens Public library under ransomware attack e-borrowing suspended
items.normalized_title: queens public library under ransomware attack e borrowing suspended
items.raw_summary: Discussed on HN Top (Queens Public library under ransomware attack e-borrowing suspended).
items.plain_english_summary: The Queens Public Library system is currently experiencing a ransomware attack that has forced the suspension of its digital borrowing services.
items.why_it_matters: This incident highlights the vulnerability of public infrastructure and digital lending ecosystems to cyber extortion, impacting community access to information.
items.who_it_is_for: Cybersecurity professionals, public sector IT administrators, and digital librarians.
items.how_it_compares: It follows a growing trend of ransomware targeting public institutions, similar to the recent attack on the British Library.
items.practical_takeaway: Organizations should ensure offline backups and incident response plans are in place for critical public-facing digital services.
items.try_it_suggestion: Monitor the library's official status page for updates on service restoration and security post-mortem details.
items.beginner_note: Ransomware is a type of malicious software that locks up a computer system's data until a payment is made to the attackers.

items.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
items.normalized_title: want to rent an internet address at the white house
items.raw_summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

items.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
items.normalized_title: tech firms dismantle botnet that turned 1 3m tv boxes into proxies
items.raw_summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

items.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
items.normalized_title: widespread php flaw may cause many site outages today
items.raw_summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.
